ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral ABCD, $AD\parallel BC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$, $BD=BC$, point E is the midpoint of CD, ray BE intersects the extension of AD at point F, connect CF. Prove that the quadrilateral BCFD is a rhombus.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution.} Proof: Since AF$\parallel$BC,\\
it follows that $\angle$DCB=$\angle$CDF, $\angle$FBC=$\angle$BFD,\\
since point E is the midpoint of CD,\\
it follows that DE=EC,\\
in $\triangle$ BCE and $\triangle$ FDE,\\
since $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle FBC=\angle BFD \\
\angle DCB=\angle CDF \\
DE=EC
\end{array}\right.$,\\
it follows that $\triangle$ BCE$\cong$ $\triangle$ FDE,\\
thus, DF=BC,\\
and since DF$\parallel$BC,\\
it follows that quadrilateral BCFD is a parallelogram,\\
since BD=BC,\\
it follows that \boxed{quadrilateral\ BCFD\ is\ a\ rhombus};

ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral ABCD, $AD\parallel BC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$, $BD=BC$, point E is the midpoint of CD, ray BE intersects the extension of AD at point F, and CF is connected. Prove that quadrilateral BCFD is a rhombus.
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution.} Proof: Since $AF\parallel BC$, it follows that $\angle DCB=\angle CDF$ and $\angle FBC=\angle BFD$. Since point E is the midpoint of CD, $DE=EC$. In $\triangle BCE$ and $\triangle FDE$, since $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle FBC=\angle BFD \\\angle DCB=\angle CDF \\\DE=EC\end{array}\right.$, it follows that $\triangle BCE\cong\triangle FDE$. Thus, $DF=BC$, and since $DF\parallel BC$, quadrilateral BCFD is a parallelogram. Since $BD=BC$, it follows that \boxed{\text{quadrilateral }BCFD\text{ is a rhombus}}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, D is on the upper line segment AF, F is at the upper right, and C is at the lower right; AD and DF are on the same straight line, and from the figure and the given conditions it can be known that BC is parallel to AD, therefore BC ∥ DF. In the figure, ray BF passes through line segment CD, and the intersection point is labeled E, so B, E, F are collinear, and C, E, D are collinear; E is the midpoint of CD, hence EC = ED. Reasoning: Consider the two groups of triangles △ECB and △EDF formed by the intersection of the two straight lines CD and BF. Because EC and ED are on the same straight line, and EB and EF are on the same straight line, ∠CEB = ∠DEF (vertical angles). Also because CB ∥ DF, and EC and ED are collinear, ∠ECB = ∠EDF. Therefore △ECB ∼ △EDF. From similarity, EC/ED = EB/EF = CB/DF can be obtained. Since E is the midpoint of CD, EC = ED, so the similarity ratio is 1, thus EB = EF, and CB = DF. In particular, E is simultaneously the midpoint of CD and BF. Thus the two diagonals CD and BF of quadrilateral BCFD bisect each other, so BCFD is a parallelogram. Finally, the given conditions give BD = BC, and BD and BC are a pair of adjacent sides of this parallelogram; if a parallelogram has one pair of adjacent sides equal, then all four sides are equal, so BCFD is a rhombus.
